article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: The first inactives are out, two questionable stars are good to go, and the board still shows last week — here's how to play Sunday.

items.headline: Lead: Madrid kicks off in about an hour — Pearce is active, Branch and Dugger are out
paragraphs: The Bengals and Falcons kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET in Madrid, and the first inactives of the day are already in. Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is active after a back injury left him questionable all week. He was activated off the suspended list on Saturday and is good to go.

Atlanta is without wide receiver Zachariah Branch with a hamstring injury, and defensive back Billy Bowman is out too. Cincinnati is without safety Kyle Dugger with a quad injury, along with center Connor Lew, offensive tackle Myles Hinton and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr. is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
The rest of the morning runs on the same clock. The early inactives land about 11:30 a.m. ET, and the late-afternoon games follow about 2:30 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: Pearce plays in Madrid; Branch, Bowman and Dugger are out — the first inactives of the day are in.

items.headline: Sunday morning answers: Egbuka and St. Brown are good to go, Monangai and Montgomery are out
paragraphs: The questionable names are resolving before the early inactives even land. Emeka Egbuka is good to go tonight against the Bears. Amon-Ra St. Brown is good to go against the Dolphins. Kyle Monangai is out once again, and David Montgomery is out with a groin injury.

Deshaun Watson is expected to be inactive at New Orleans even after clearing the concussion protocol, so Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland and Dillon Gabriel is the No. 2. Dolphins running back Jaylen Wright is out with a quad injury against Detroit.

Still open: George Pickens with a hamstring injury and Jake Ferguson with an ankle injury. The Cowboys elevated a wide receiver and a tight end from the practice squad on Saturday, which is a tell that one or both could sit. Their status resolves at the early inactives, about 11:30 a.m. ET.

Friday's designations still stand behind all of this: Cam Skattebo is doubtful, Rashid Shaheed, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Deebo Samuel, Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, Garrett Wilson and A.J. Brown are out, and Breece Hall is back after five games out.
items.takeaway: Egbuka and St. Brown play; Monangai, Montgomery and Wright sit; Sanders starts with Watson inactive — Pickens and Ferguson resolve at 11:30 a.m. ET.

items.headline: Weather: still calm — no wind flags for Sunday
paragraphs: The final forecast held overnight. No Week 9 game is flagged for wind. This morning's check has Seattle at 10 mph sustained wind with gusts to 15 mph and a 10 percent chance of light rain, and Chicago at 10 mph sustained wind with gusts to 17 mph at 51 degrees under a clear sky.
The Madrid game plays under a retractable roof, and Cleveland at New Orleans and Monday night's Bills-Vikings game are indoors. Nothing in the forecast changes how a game plays.
items.takeaway: Sunday is calm: no wind flags, gusts top out in the teens, and the Madrid game plays under a roof.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: Read again this morning, the app board still shows Week 8, generated November 2. There are no Week 9 cards at all. It has not flipped, and it has not picked up any of the Sunday quarterback changes.

The quarterback fields are stale across the board. Philadelphia still lists Tanner McKee, but Joe Milton III starts today. Cleveland still lists Deshaun Watson, but he is expected to be inactive and Shedeur Sanders starts. Seattle still lists Sam Darnold, but he is out and Drew Lock starts. If you read a Sunday quarterback off this board, you are reading last week.

So there is still no Sunday card to read, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Sunday's prices go through Check until the board flips.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets — two numbers that tell different stories
paragraphs: Every betting split has two numbers. Tickets are the share of bets — how many people are on a side. Handle is the share of money — how many dollars are on a side. When they point the same way, the crowd and the cash agree. When they split, they are telling different stories.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say 70 percent of the bets are on the favorite, but only 40 percent of the money is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite and fewer, bigger bets on the underdog. It does not prove the underdog is the right side. It just means the money is not following the crowd.

Why it matters: a split between tickets and handle is the first thing to look for when you hear someone talk about fading the public. If both numbers are on the same side, there is no disagreement to fade — just a popular team.
items.takeaway: Tickets count the bets, handle counts the money — when they disagree, the money is telling a different story than the crowd, and that is where a Fade starts.

items.headline: Overnight was quiet — one small drift in Detroit
paragraphs: Nothing big moved overnight. The lines the evening brief flagged are sitting in the same place this morning: the Giants are still -3 against Philadelphia, the total is still 38.5, the Chiefs-Jets total is still 48.5, and the Madrid total is still 52.5.

The one drift is Detroit. The Lions went from -7 to -6.5 against Miami, and the total slipped from 50 to 49.5. Dallas is -5.5 on the consensus board this morning after DraftKings showed -4.5 on Saturday — if your book still shows -4.5, that is the number to run through Check.

The app board has not picked up any of this yet, because it still shows Week 8. So if your book has one of these numbers and it looks good to you, run it through Check. Type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Overnight was quiet — Giants -3, Chiefs total 48.5 and the Madrid total 52.5 all held; only Detroit drifted, to -6.5.

items.headline: Sunday morning is for Check — bet the good number, wait only on Pickens and Ferguson
paragraphs: The first inactives are already in for Madrid, and the early inactives land about 11:30 a.m. ET. The only real reason to wait this morning is a game where you are specifically waiting on a questionable name — George Pickens or Jake Ferguson in Dallas. There, the inactive list is a real pending event, and it is worth the wait.

Everywhere else, do not keep waiting for a better price that may never come. If your book has a Sunday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number this afternoon, because the Sunday rush on big-name teams can push a line past the app's playable number just as easily as it can push it your way.

A quick price reminder: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be. And a note on the tracker: settlement is manual, so log the losers too — the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself.
items.takeaway: Run your book's Sunday price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now; wait only on Pickens and Ferguson.
